title: Makarba, on Ahmedabad's south-western edge
caption: Makarba is recorded as a census town in Ahmedabad district, home to 18,090 people at the 2001 census. Sarkhej Roza stands within it.

title: Sarkhej Roza
caption: A tomb built in honour of the Sufi saint Shaikh Ahmed Khattu Ganj Bakhsh, begun in 1445 and completed in 1451, later greatly expanded by Sultan Mahmud Begada. A Monument of National Importance.

title: Sarkhej Lake
caption: A lake of about 6.9 hectares, dug under Mahmud Begada and surrounded with cut stone steps, with his palace at its south-west corner.

title: The junction carts
caption: Fruit and sugarcane carts beside the shrine approach, busiest from Thursday to Sunday, balancing trade against traffic.

title: Highway, bus stand and autos
caption: The Sarkhej–Gandhinagar Highway runs about 44.5 km north to Gandhinagar.

title: Canal bank and factory road
caption: An evening walk along the canal bank, and a vending stretch on the factory road that grew over about five years.

title: Old cotton-mill site
caption: A former mill compound. Ahmedabad's textile mills earned it the name "Manchester of India", and several later closed.
